title: Short exact cylinder presentation preserving all three components
statement: For an abelian category C with a derived category, a strict square tβ=αt′ of integer cochain maps admits short exact cylinder rows A→T→Cone(t) and A′→T′→Cone(t′) and a row morphism m. Six localized isomorphisms identify the rows with A,B,Cone(t) and A′,B′,Cone(t′). The horizontal maps become t,t′ and cone inclusions, and ALL three vertical components become α, β and the functorial cone map, respectively.

source.place: Tag 014D, Lemma 13.9.6 and the explicit cylinder construction; also the existing proved ConeDiagramSESPresentation implementation.

proof.text: For each arrow t put T=B⊕Cone(id A), i=(t,0,id), and q(b,a⁺,a)=(-a⁺,b-t(a)). The cone differential verifies that these are chain maps and iq=0. The degreewise retraction r(b,a⁺,a)=a and section s(a⁺,b)=(b,-a⁺,0) satisfy ir=id, sq=id, and ri+qs=id, so the row A→T→Cone(t) is degreewise split short exact.

The identity cone has its standard contracting homotopy. Localization kills all maps out of it, so Q of the projection T→B is an isomorphism with inverse Q of the B inclusion. Under this comparison the first arrow is Q(t), and the second is the cone inclusion; the extra identity-cone summand maps to zero.

Use β on B and the functorial cone map induced by α on Cone(id A) to map the source cylinder to the target cylinder. The given strict-square equation makes this commute with i and q. On A it is α and on the quotient it is the standard cone map. The six comparisons, identity at first and third vertices and the projection comparison at middle vertices, give the result.
The middle cylinder map is biprod.map β (Cone.map α α). Composing with the target projection gives the source projection followed by β. Applying Q proves the extra middle-component identity.

theorem cone_diagram_full_ses_presentation
    {C : Type u} [Category C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C]
    (A B A' B' : CochainComplex C ℤ)
    (t : A ⟶ B) (t' : A' ⟶ B') (α : A ⟶ A') (β : B ⟶ B')
    (hc : t ≫ β = α ≫ t') :
    ∃ (P P' : ShortComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ)) (m : P ⟶ P')
      (d₁ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.X₁ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj A)
      (d₂ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.X₂ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj B)
      (d₃ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.X₃ ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone t))
      (d₁' : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P'.X₁ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj A')
      (d₂' : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P'.X₂ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj B')
      (d₃' : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P'.X₃ ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone t')),
      P.ShortExact ∧ P'.ShortExact ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map P.f ≫ d₂.hom = d₁.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map t ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map P.g ≫ d₃.hom =
        d₂.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr t) ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map P'.f ≫ d₂'.hom = d₁'.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map t' ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map P'.g ≫ d₃'.hom =
        d₂'.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr t') ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map m.τ₁ ≫ d₁'.hom = d₁.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map α ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map m.τ₂ ≫ d₂'.hom = d₂.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map β ∧
      DerivedCategory.Q.map m.τ₃ ≫ d₃'.hom =
        d₃.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mappingCone.map t t' α β hc)
